mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 3% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% MoM does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a reduction in consumer demand, which leads to lower corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants react to the positive economic news.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% MoM does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the easing monetary policy, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 MoM does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% YoY, it indicates a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and GDPC1 growth < 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of HOUST decline > 10% YoY and GDPC1 growth < 2% YoY does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth is above 3% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy environment with high inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with high inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 3% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).
